Robert Wright
Deputy CFO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you for standing by. My name is Jayl, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the DK Q4 2024 Earnings Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speaker's remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, simply press star followed by the number 1 on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, simply press star one again. I would now like to turn the conference over to Robert Wright, Deputy CFO. You may begin.
Good morning and welcome to the Delek US Q4 Earnings Conference Call. Participants joining me on today's call will include Avigdor Sorek, President and CEO, Joseph Israel, EVP Operations, Reuven Spiegel, EVP and Chief Financial Officer, and Mark Hobbs, EVP Corporate Development. Today's presentation material can be found on the investor relations section of the Delek US website. Slide two contains our safe harbor statement regarding forward-looking comments. Any forward-looking information shared during today's call will involve risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from today's comments. Factors that could cause actual results to differ are included here as well as within our SEC filings. The company assumes no obligation to update any forward-looking statements. I will now turn the call over to Avigdor for opening remarks. Avigdor.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Robert. Good morning and thank you for joining us today. Despite the challenging refining margin environment, which we believe was around $6 below mid-cycle in Q4 of 2024 was transformational year for us. We have vastly improved our operational performance, made significant progress on some of the past efforts, and implemented key plans to increase the overall profitability of our company. I would like to highlight the progress we have made on our key priorities. First, safe and reliable operations. We have made great progress in improving the operations towards our company. We have successfully completed a major turnaround at Krotz Springs in Q4. Coming out of the turnaround, the refinery is showing improved operational performance. The asset is running well, and we look forward to a strong contribution from Krotz Springs in 2025. Moving to Big Spring.
In 2024, we have significantly improved its reliability. We have consistently been running over 70,000 barrels per day. Looking forward, in 2025, we have no major turnarounds planned in our system, and we expect to continue our improvement journey. Now, I would like to discuss our sum of the parts strategy. In 2024, we made great progress in unlocking the sum of the parts value inherent in our assets. In September, we sold our retail asset for $390 million, and we are extremely happy with the timing and the value we received. The timely sale has allowed us to continue to progress our initiative in a tough refining environment. We have also made great progress in making Delek Logistics a strong independent midstream company levered to the growth in the Permian Basin.
In 2024, we successfully executed economic swap of assets between DK and DKL. The swap will improve the profitability of our refineries going forward. At the same time, the swap bring more certainty to DKL cash flow through the contract extension by up to seven years. Our economic separation from DKL is increasing, and at the same time, the distribution DK received from DKL continue to grow. DKL also announced two accretive acquisitions to add around $100 million in third-party EBITDA. After DKL acquisition of Gravity Water Midstream, DK ownership in DKL has come down to 63.6%. DKL is progressing its capacity expansion in the Libby Gas Processing Complex and expect to complete the expansion in the first half of 2025, as previously communicated. Additionally, DKL announced an FID on acid gas injection at the Libby complex in December.
These steps highlight DKL's progress in becoming an attractive, high-growth, mid-sized midstream company, benefiting from the natural gas growth in the Permian Basin. This is reflected in the strong guidance that Delek Logistics has provided today. Despite this great move, DKL continue to trade at discount versus its peers, and very limited, if any, of this value is reflected in DK shares. We are in the process of taking additional steps such that the value of greater than $350 million in third-party EBITDA in DKL is fully reflected in DK share price and DKL unit price. We are confident that we'll complete the DKL deconsolidation in methodical manner and create value for both shareholders and unitholders. In 2024, we have made progress in improving overall profitability of the company.
We completed our zero-based budget initiative, which allowed us to save around $100 million in cost through our system. We completed this program in Q2 2024, ahead of our original target of completion by the end of 2024. Our ZBB effort laid the foundation for our enterprise optimization plan or EOP. EOP aims to improve DK cash flow by $80 to 120 million per year, starting in the H2 of 2025. I'm pleased to announce that we have made great progress with EOP, and now we expect to be closer to the top end of our cash flow improvement guidance. Despite our initial success, we are not standing still and look forward for further improve our cash generation power as we progress through the year.
Final piece of our strategy is being shareholder-friendly and having a strong balance sheet. During the quarter, we paid $16 million in dividends and bought back $22 million of our shares. We remain committed to a disciplined and balanced approach to capital allocation. Now, I would like to make a comment about small refinery exemption. As you know, the D.C. Circuit Court overturned the EPA denial of our small refinery exemption petition under the RFS in July 2024. Our petitions were sent back to the EPA for reconsideration. We're optimistic that the EPA will revise its approach following the court ruling and grant us SREs. We hope the recent ruling on SREs, along with Supreme Court ruling on Chevron deference case, will reduce unneeded bureaucracy and allow for a predictable approach to the SRE petition review.
In closing, I would like to thank our entire team for the hard work and dedication. We are excited about the prospects of DK in 2025 and beyond. Now, I will turn the call over to Joseph, who will provide additional color on our operations.
Joseph Israel
EVP of operations, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Avigal. First, I'd like to congratulate our team on another safe, reliable, and environmentally compliant year. Our progress in hiring the right people, developing good processes, and proactively managing our equipment is well reflected in the field and is giving us a strong foundation to perform, optimize, and grow our business. In Tyler, total throughput in Q4 was approximately 66,000 barrels per day. Production margin in the quarter was $6.66 per barrel, and operating expenses were $5.51 per barrel. During Q1, we are executing our plant maintenance in the Alky unit, including an upgrade scope, which will allow us to increase production of high-value products by approximately 500 barrels per day. For Q1, our estimated total throughput in Tyler is in the 65,000 to 69,000 barrels per day range.
In El Dorado, total throughput in Q4 was approximately 77,000 barrels per day. Our production margin was $0.56 per barrel, and operating expenses were $4.78 per barrel. Estimated throughput for Q1 is in the 73,000 to 76,000 barrels per day range. On the strategic front, we are making good progress with our EOP initiatives, which are expected to add, by mid-year, $50 million of annual EBITDA run rate in the El Dorado integrated system. The incremental, approximately $2 per barrel of net margin, will support El Dorado cash flow generation through the cycles. In Big Spring, total throughput for the quarter was approximately 73,000 barrels per day.
Our production margin was $5.04 per barrel, and operating expenses were $6.29 per barrel, including approximately $0.50 per barrel of winterization and maintenance special activities. Progress in Big Spring is well reflected in the numbers. Total throughput in 2024 increased over 10% compared to 2023 due to improved reliability. Cost structure is approaching our target, and as important, it is mostly driven now by routine and proactive agenda rather than reactive. In Q1, we are replacing catalyst in our reformer and diesel hydrotreater per plan. As a result, estimated throughput for Q1 is in the 57,000 to 61,000 barrels per day range. In Krotz Springs, the team successfully completed the planned major turnaround. Since startup, we have demonstrated improved crude capacity, product mix, and liquid yield recovery capabilities consistent with our plans.
Total throughput in Q4 was approximately 50,000 barrels per day. Our production margin was $2.71 per barrel, and operating expenses in Q4 were $5.27 per barrel. Our planned throughput for Q1 is in the 83,000 to 86,000 barrels per day range. Our implied system throughput target for Q1 is in the 278,000 to 292,000 barrels per day range. Moving on to the commercial front. In Q4, supply and marketing contributed a loss of $34.6 million. Of that, approximately $12 million loss was generated by wholesale marketing, driven by seasonal low demand trends around our system racks. $22 million loss was attributed to supply, and a negative $0.5 million contribution was generated by asphalt.
In summary, we continue to execute well on the fundamentals of our business. After successfully addressing reliability gaps, our teams continue to focus on operational excellence and commercial optimization initiatives as we position ourselves for the coming gasoline season and the future cycles. I will now turn the call over to Robert Wright for the financial variances.
Robert Wright
Deputy CFO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Joseph. I will start by referring to slide 14. For Q4, Delek had a net loss of $414 million or negative $6.55 per share. Included within this is a partial impairment of our goodwill balance of $212 million. Adjusted net loss was $161 million or negative $2.54 per share, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $23 million. On slide 15, the waterfall of adjusted EBITDA from Q3 2024 to Q4 2024 shows that the decline is primarily because of lower refining contributions. The $80 million decrease in refining is primarily attributable to a lower margin environment in Q4 relative to the third quarter.
As to the logistics segment, we continue to have another strong quarter, delivering $107 million in adjusted EBITDA. Moving to slide 16 to discuss cash flow. Cash flow from operations was a use of $164 million. Within this amount is our net loss for the period, in addition to an outflow of approximately $71 million of timing related working capital movements, which include the impacts of the inventory intermediation agreement. Investing activities of $216 million includes capital asset purchases of $191 million and a $23 million deposit paid for the Gravity acquisition, which closed on 2 January 2025. Financing activities of $77 million reflects the DK equity offering and timing of accruals.
This also includes $22 million in share repurchases, $16 million in dividend payments, and $19 million in distribution payments. On slide 17, we have the actual results of the 2024 capital program. Q4 capital expenditures were $198 million. $140 million of this spend was in the refining segment, a large portion of which was related to the successful completion of the Krotz Springs turnaround. The remaining amount is largely spend associated with the construction of the Libby Two gas plant, which remains on track from a timing and cost perspective. As we have previously announced, our standalone DK capital outlook for 2025 is approximately $150 to 170 million. Our net cash position is broken out between Delek and Delek Logistics on slide 18.
During the quarter, we drew approximately $300 million of cash, primarily due to anticipated capital expenditures on growth projects and the turnaround at KSR. Additional unfavorable impacts included working capital timing differences and the overall market conditions impacting our recognized EBITDA results for the period. Excluding Delek Logistics, we finished the year with an increase of $82 million in net debt. We are pleased with the relatively modest increase in net debt for the year, especially considering the broader market conditions and the impact on our peers, many of whom have experienced substantial increases. Moving now to slide 19, where we cover outlook items. In addition to the guidance Joseph provided, for Q1 2025, we expect operating expenses to be between $220 and $235 million. G&A to be between $55 and $60 million.
D&A is expected to be between $100 and 105 million, and net interest expense to be between $78 and 88 million. We will now open the call for questions.
Operator
Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. If you have dialed in and would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad to raise your hand and join the queue. If you would like to withdraw your question, simply press star one again. If you're called upon to ask a question and are listening via loudspeaker on your device, please pick up your handset and ensure that your phone is not on mute when asking a question. We do request for today's session that you please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Your first question comes from the line of Manav Gupta of UBS. Your line is open.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Morning, guys. I wanted to focus on a little bit on slide 10. Obviously, you are making a lot of improvements on El Dorado. Help us understand what more can be done to make this a truly competitive asset, something which can be performing in line with probably Tyler here, at least.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Manav, good morning. Thank you for your question. El Dorado is a big focus for us. Joseph's leading that with a lot of talent, and I will allow Joseph to chime in.
Joseph Israel
EVP of operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. The El Dorado is the most significant beneficiary of our EOP focus on the product mix. We started to make and sell jet fuel through the rack. We are looking to convert heavy bottoms to light products. Process efficiency, we are focused on liquid yield recovery, mainly in the reformer, FCC, and asphalt areas. On the logistics front, we put together new logistics, and we are already shipping more products away from the local market to optimize the net backs. Bottom line, Manav, considering our strong refinery team out there, the asset flexibility and the $50 million of low-hanging fruits, we are confident about our ability to translate this progress to numbers sooner than later.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Perfect, guys. Quick follow-up here is, looks like you're growing DKL EBITDA, although you're, you know, you're divesting it down slowly. Is the strategy here to look for smaller bolt-on deals, whether it's water, crude, gas, and basically continue to grow the company at the DKL level, and at the same time try and bring down the ownership below 50%?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Manav, I will take that question. I would like to give you a bigger answer than that about some of the path forward we are doing. Some of the path forward together with EOP are the most strategic initiative we have for this year. Right? Deconsolidation, I want to make it crystal clear, is happening and will happen as we speak. It's very, very clear. I want to take a moment and reflect on 2024 actions that we did around it, right? In 2024, we sold retail as we wanted. We continued to make progress in the deconsolidation. Right? We took the ownership of that from 79 to below 64% today.
We grew the EBITDA while we are doing all of that from 385 not very long ago to over 400 this year, the 2024 to 500 guidance for 2025, which is another step. We increased the third-party EBITDA from 40% to 70%. Manav, while we were doing all of that, we also increased the distribution that DK gets from DKL. It's many boxes that we are checking the box on. Today, I don't know if you know this, we announced another efficient tool in our toolbox to allow basically efficient tax way for DK to sell back their units to DKL. We announced it today for up to $150 million.
That's benefit for DK for the efficient way, and it's also benefit for DKL because of free cash flow, right? You are borrowing at seven, and you are avoiding a cost of 10 or 11. That's very beneficial for both companies. The last point I wanna make that the deconsolidation is the goal of both companies because it will allow DKL to grow over time and then allow DK to get the whole value in the asset. With that said, Mark was very busy this year, with all the deals we had, and the plan is that he was gonna be very busy in 2025 as well. I'll let Mark chime in.
Mark Hobbs
EVP Corporate Development, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Thanks, Avigal. Look, Manav, we're very happy with our sum of the parts efforts in 2024. We were very active in the year in advancing our deconsolidation efforts. You know, both H2O and Gravity checked all the boxes in what we look at for acquisitions. You know, highly strategic and highly synergistic with our Midland Basin operations and what we're trying to do out there as a full-service midstream provider. Immediately accreted to free cash flow, improved our leverage, and increased our coverage ratio. We also initiated organic growth projects in the Delaware to add to our gas processing capacity and to also add critical sour gas capabilities. Finally, dropped down Wink to Webster, our 15% interest in Wink to Webster.
When you take all of those combined, we're adding significant third-party EBITDA to DKL, which is driving this economic separation between DK and DKL that we're talking about. If you layer on top of that, we also continue to see premium valuations paid in the private markets, by midstream companies for midstream assets over the past few months, and in particular, those tied to the Permian Basin, which, as you know, is the core of our DKL operations. As Avigal said, our focus is that we're gonna continue our measured approach to deconsolidation, and the focus is gonna continue on enhancing and maximizing value for both DK shareholders and DKL unitholders.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Thank you, guys.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Matthew Blair of TPH&Co. Your line is open.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH&Co.
Thank you, and good morning. I was hoping to go into the supply and marketing dynamics a little bit more in Q4. I understand there's some seasonality with wholesale, but could you help us understand why is that just an outright negative EBITDA contribution, and does there need to be any structural changes there? Then how are these supply and marketing dynamics trending so far in Q1? Thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Hey, Matt. Good morning. Thank you for the question. First of all, I'm very happy on the progress that DKL are doing. If you are comparing that to the Q4 of last year, the market condition back then was better versus this quarter, but DKL achieved $10 million better this quarter versus last quarter. That's a very good step on the right direction. I will let Patrick Reilly, our Chief Commercial Officer, to chime in into that answer and give you some color. Go ahead.
Patrick Reilly
Chief Commercial Officer, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Avigal. Q4 DKL performance was impacted primarily by seasonal inland demand weakness led by the Group three and a one-time major turnaround across. With that said, DKL made significant progress on our 2024 initiatives. As Avigal just mentioned, supply and trading market conditions in Q4 were significantly weaker relative to the same time period in 2023. As an example, Group three diesel weakened by $0.14 per gallon. That's almost $6 a barrel year-on-year. Now, despite these headwinds, DKL outperformed Q4 2023 by nearly $10 million. DKL will play a crucial role in the delivery of the 2025 EOP, and our strategy is actually simple.
Mark Hobbs
EVP Corporate Development, Delek US Holdings
To intelligently streamline operations, thereby reducing costs, further increase our margins on the back of optimization of supply and trading, lean into our partnership with our assets to flex our broader product offering, and further mature DKL's newfound and expanded market reach. We're excited for the commitment and the challenge.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH&Co.
Sounds good. On the RD side, have you made a decision on whether to invest in the Bakersfield renewable diesel plant?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. That's not on our table this 10 seconds. If something change, we'll definitely let you know, but it's not. Maybe Mohit, you wanna chime in on that?
Mohit Bhardwaj
SVP of Strategy and Growth, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Matt, that option is still available to us, as you and I have discussed in the past. The team over there has to show that they have had healthy operations for around 3 months, and then we have around 90 days to exercise our option. We are obviously going to be looking at it once we are asked to look at that option. As of right now, that option is still available to us, and we're just hoping for the team to have those operations in order before we start making our decisions.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH&Co.
Sounds good. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of John Royall of JP Morgan. Your line is open.
John Royall
Executive Director, JP Morgan
Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking my question.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Hey, John. Good morning.
John Royall
Executive Director, JP Morgan
My first question's on the OpEx guide for Q1. We noticed a step up from where you had guided to Q4, but it's also in the context of things going well with EOP. I was hoping you could help us bridge the difference and maybe how should we think about that OpEx number as we progress further into 2025 beyond that Q1 guide?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Absolutely, John. Thank you for the question. Mohit was putting the guidance together, so I will let him chime in. Please, Mohit.
Mohit Bhardwaj
SVP of Strategy and Growth, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, John, thanks for the question. So as far as our company is concerned, OpEx and cost reduction, we are taking a lot of pride in it. You know, you're seeing the results through EOP. You have seen the results through ZBB. As far as your specific question around Q1 guidance is concerned, there are four factors which are influencing the guidance. The first one is, as you know, that we closed Gravity Water Midstream, and we presented the guidance on a consolidated basis. You're seeing some OpEx coming from Gravity Water Midstream. Second, you know, we are running higher throughput quarter-over-quarter, so that's also influencing our, you know, OpEx number. Third piece is natural gas. As you've seen, natural gas prices have gone a little bit higher, so that's also influencing our OpEx numbers.
Finally, we have some planned maintenance at Big Spring in Q1, which is reflected in our throughput guidance. That is also impacting our overall OpEx. As I started my answer, OpEx and cost reduction is an extremely positive story for Delek. We're very excited about how, you know, OpEx reductions are contributing to EOP and our free cash flow generation, and we look forward to updating you guys more on that.
John Royall
Executive Director, JP Morgan
Great. Very helpful. Thanks, Mohit. Then, my follow-up's another one on guidance. Maybe just on the DKL EBITDA guidance. Just trying to bridge from the run rate of about, I think, it's about $430 million annually in Q4 to this guide that's about $50 to 90 million above that. If you could just walk us through some of those moving pieces. I know obviously there's Gravity, there's the gas plant coming on mid-year, you know, maybe some other things on the organic side. Just a little bit of detail on how you get from the 430 to 480 to 520.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, absolutely. First of all, John, we need to take a step back and talk about DKL in a broader context. DKL is a growing story, and obviously, as we speak, we are increasing the economic separation between the companies, and we are doing that very methodically and to benefit both unitholder and shareholder, as you see by all the action that we have done in the last 18 months or so. That, that's very, very important. We decided to allow you guys to have guidance for DKL because we want everyone to model that company right and to be able to understand the value creation that was done here. We're taking a lot of pride of what we are doing here. We think the guidance we gave you is solid and good.
Mohit, do you wanna chime into that as well? If there is more, modeling question, we can take it offline, obviously.
Mohit Bhardwaj
SVP of Strategy and Growth, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, I think Avigal, you covered most of it. John, I can definitely help you walk through the moving pieces. You know, we can do a one-on-one call after this. Maybe we should take that offline.
John Royall
Executive Director, JP Morgan
Great. Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Doug Leggate of Wolfe Research. Your line is open.
Doug Leggate
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, Wolfe Research
Hi, this is McKinley, on for Doug. He sends his regards. He's traveling at the moment. My first question kind of piggybacks on some of the commentary that's already been had. In addition to the EOP, you guys have quite a few options in terms of being able to release value from DKL. Where are you in the process, for example, with the sour gas permitting? And is there a kind of line of sight on potentially other sellable assets going forward?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. You started your question with EOP, so I will start my answer.
Doug Leggate
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, Wolfe Research
Yes.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
with EOP. I will give you some more, broader context around it. So especially on the refinery environment that we are at, EOP is all about free cash flow, period, end of story. That's what we are after, right? We obviously today is a happy day around it because we felt comfortable enough to take our guidance towards the end of the range we gave in the past. So that's a happy moment for us. We have seen a significant progress on the cost side already been signed, and we'll see them executed and coming to fruition over the next few months. As Pat mentioned, we see a good progress also on the margin improvement that we see on EOP. I wanna ensure you that we are not stopping here. We're not standing still.
We always have more options and more things that we are working on and adding to that very important initiative, and we are very optimistic about that. The last comment I want to make that it's pretty neutral to market condition and all the actions that we are doing here are new action that was not done in the past. We are very optimistic. Reuven is very close to that, and help managing that very nicely, and I will let him chime in on that.
Reuven Spiegel
EVP and CFO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Avigal. The EOP plan includes a bank of projects from all areas of the company, and I will address specifically your question about DKL at the end. Each project has to be validated two ways. One, that it's sustainable, and two, that is, for the most part, market agnostic. Once vetted, it builds into execution and added to the projections. You can see on the deck that were provided, it's reflected in slide 9 in the green boxes. Each project has a different time frame for fruition. That is why we're measuring Q3 and Q4 run rates. As for DKL, we have the sour gas plant, which our team is executing on time, on budget, and is expected to flow in Q2.
That gives us a whole new dimension and flexibility around gas, sorry.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you for-
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Jason Gabelman of TD Cowen. Your line is open.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Yeah. Hey, morning. Thanks for taking my question.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Hey, Jason. Good morning. Thanks for joining us today.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Research Analyst, TD Cowen
I wanted to ask about the DKL repurchase program of DK units. I'm wondering, one, what the timeline is to deploy that buyback cash. Two, once DK gets that cash, what it's gonna use that cash for.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Thank you for the question. The timeline that we put that program in is all the way up till 2026. Obviously, it's a DKL option, but we are very close to that, so we'll do that when time is right. You probably can appreciate that that's another tool in our toolbox, that benefit the deconsolidation for both companies and helps free cash flow of both companies. That checks many, many boxes. It's very tax efficient. I think you can be proud of a very creative way how to create deconsolidation with no tax impact, basically. I wanna take the other part and to talk about the capital allocation program we have. I wanna give a broader discussion around that.
We said many times, and we are saying that today, that we are maintaining dividends throughout the cycle. We are doing that. We've done that, and we will do it in the future. We have a balanced approach between taking care of the balance sheet and buyback. We did buyback in Q3, we did buyback in Q4, and we are doing buyback at Q1 of 2025. At the current valuation of our share price, we see a huge value in our share price, and we are acting on that, just to make it very clear. That's kind of, that's where we are.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Great. No, yeah, appreciate the color on the capital allocation. The other question is just back to Group three dynamics, and it sounds like in a weaker inland margin environment, you see some weakness in that supply line item. I wonder, you know, kind of post-COVID, we've seen inland markets become more seasonal, where they're weaker in the winter. Should we expect that supply line is weaker in Q4 and Q1 kind of in line where it was this past quarter or maybe, I guess, a little better, based on what's gone on in the EOP program? Or I guess, how should we think about the seasonality of that supply line? Thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Listen, there are two different questions here. A market observation, there is some truth that there is a weakness in the winter and a strength in the summer. We are not gonna provide guidance for DKL. We didn't do this in the past, and I don't think it's best practice in the market. We are not gonna deviate from that today. I'm gonna tell you, and Jason, you need to know this very well, that we are moving very well with the things that we are controlling, like different products that we are starting to move and different markets that we are moving towards. I can be only very pleased with the progress we are doing about what we can control. I will leave it at that.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Okay. Understood. Thanks for the answers.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Good.
Operator
That concludes our Q&A session. I will now turn the conference back over to Avigal Soreq for closing remarks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I would like to thank my colleagues around the table for a great, safe, and reliable year. I want to thank the entire Delek employees for a great execution and a great commitment for the company, and I'm very pleased with that. To thank our board of directors and to thank you, investors, for believing in our story and our journey. With that, I would conclude the call, and we'll see you next in the next quarter. Thank you.
Operator
This concludes today's conference call. You may now disconnect.

As of now, that is all the effort essentially done, and other than, say, you're talking about how you may be still looking at sending different product to a different market. Other than that, from a manufacturing standpoint, is all the changes or all the improvement you're trying to make already done at this point?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I think on the cost structure, we guided the market to $5.50 target, and this quarter, we are about $0.85 per barrel over that in Big Spring. The reason is we have several special programs still going on for a long-term improvements. As they go away by year-end, we will be at the $5.50 target, and we believe that will be sustainable. Now, the point I made before, when you stop playing defense, you can start working on your offense. We have a lot of great ideas in Big Spring. It's a great asset, and we have a lot of room there on the octane side and the feedstock side that we will look very closely and move forward.
Paul Cheng
Anayst, Scotiabank
All right. Will do. Thank you.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
We do have our last question, comes from the line of Jason Gabelman with TD Cowen. Your line is open.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director and Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Yeah. Hey, thanks for taking my questions. Apologies, I'm gonna try this again on what Paul just asked in terms of some of the EBITDA contributions. If I look at what you've disclosed for the DKL transactions, H2O is $45 million of EBITDA. The gas processing plant, call it $25, $30 million of EBITDA. That kinda gets you to that projected $70 million of EBITDA for DKL. It implies that then Wink to Webster offsets the DK contract amend and extend. Is that the right math, or is there something off there?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Jason, I think it's a good opportunity to do a follow-up with Mohit. We see more value in the gas plant, for example, and there is more EBITDA that comes back between DKL back to DK. I said that to Paul. It's around $60 million over time. It's not all of that day one. We didn't give specific numbers on each one of the transactions, and that's the reason we made sure that the strategy is clear to you and others, that we want to make sure that the right ownership is on the right place, and we are improving capture rate while growing DKL. That's the objective.
If you look at it holistically, we tried, I think we achieved for the most part, to achieve on the same quarter, deconsolidation ready, while making a clearer separation between companies. That's what we're after. That's, in our mind, a very, very important step, both for stakeholder and unitholder.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director and Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay. When you say $60 million of value over time, how many years do you expect that to take?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
We're not gonna get into the details, but I encourage you to get with Mohit and get some more detailed question.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director and Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay. My other question is just once again on use of proceeds. You know, your interest expenses, it looks pretty high right now and in terms of improving the cash flow of the parent company, it seems like that's a great place to attack. Is that kind of priority one, and why is there hesitance right now in just kind of talking through the use of proceeds? Thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
The use of proceeds is according to our strategy, and obviously when we are looking on free cash flow, we always look at it on mid-cycle. Mid-cycle free cash flow looks great to our expectation. We have ability to do everything we need and to have a good return to invest also. We are very confident in the where we are and looking forward.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director and Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay. Thanks for the answers, and I'll follow up offline.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
That concludes the question and answer session. Mr. Avigal Soreq, our CEO. I turn the call back over to you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Thank you for joining us today. Thank you for the management team around the table for the extreme focus and execution around here. Thank you for our employees, the board of directors, you, the investor, and a special thank you for the retail employees for a long time being with us. Welcome to the H2O team that are joining our family today. We'll talk again in the next quarter. Thank you.
Operator
This concludes today's conference call. You may now disconnect.

content.text:
Operator
First question will come from the line of Neil Mehta with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Good morning, Avigal team.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Morning to you. How are you?
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Good morning, sir. Couple of questions for you on the guide. The first is just capital program. To Reuven's point, Q1 of $46 million versus a full year of $330 million. Are you tracking inside of that $330 million? Is capital efficiency positively surprising, recognizing you've got the Krotz Springs turnaround? The related question to that is you've got a big turnaround across this year, later this year. How do you define success? Because I think that'll be an important test for that asset.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. First of all, thank you for the question. It's still early in the year. We are not changing our guidance. At this point, we are still with the $330 million we mentioned. In terms of the success of the KSR turnaround, I would give that three elements, right? First of all, is safety. We need to make sure that it's a safe turnaround, that everyone come back home the same way they went back to work. That's number one. Second is the scope of the work. We need to make sure that we are doing the scope right and getting the uplift of the $30 million we said before. The third, obviously, is the cost. Those are the three components.
We demonstrate to ourselves doing the Tyler turnaround, we can achieve all of those three, and we aim to achieve those in this turnaround as well.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thanks, Avigal. You indicated you initiated a process to unlock the value of the retail business. You know, can you talk about how it came to the decision that this makes sense to potentially monetize and where we are with the process? Are there any synergies in your early look at this process?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thanks, Neil. I will answer the question more widely about the sum of the parts efforts that we are obviously trying to do. As you probably mentioned in the call, we created the third-party value over time, and that's obviously something that is very important for us to achieve. We are committed to make sure that that value is achieved at all times. We demonstrate during this quarter that the financial strength of the DKL balance sheet is there in order to support it. That's point number two. The point number three is that we wanna make sure that the value is being created both for the DK shareholder and the DKL unit holder, and both the units show the full value.
We obviously, as we mentioned, shared that we started the formal process. The process goes as planned. I don't know, Mark, maybe you want to...
Mark Hobbs
EVP and CFO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, sure, Avigal. I'll touch on the sum of the parts initiatives as well. I just touch a few things here. You know, as Avigal mentioned earlier on the call, you know, our belief is that in order for us to highlight the hidden value that we have in the attractive midstream position that we built, in particular in the Permian Basin, we need to find the right ownership structure, you know, for those assets. I think as we've discussed clearly on prior calls, you know, we've evaluated all the options that are in front of us, the governance and tax implications of each of those.
We still wanna stress that in any action that we take ultimately on the midstream side, you know, we are focused and laser focused on ensuring that we make both Delek and Delek Logistics stronger entities from a cash flow and leverage standpoint. We don't wanna move away from that position, and that's what we're focused on. You know, on the retail front, you know, as Avigal mentioned, we have mandated an investment bank to work with us on evaluating those strategic options that are in front of us for that business. You know, things are progressing well on that front. You know, we don't have anything specific that we wanna say today, but we will come back to you know, hopefully in the near future, with some more color on that.
You know, to your point, the way that we're envisioning this is that we don't see any significant or particular dis-synergies associated with anything that we do on that front.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thank you, Mark.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Roger Read with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Yeah, thank you. Good morning.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Morning.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Maybe a little bit, I'm gonna kind of follow up on Neil's. I mean, what is the right way to think about use of funds from retail disposition or anything else? I mean, I'm thinking, you know, even wider. You've got your ownership and Wink to Webster that's held inside of DK relative to, you know, probably belongs more in a midstream sort of operation. Maybe a little more of your thoughts as you rearrange some of the pieces here to achieve that upside value for both DK and DKL. Where should we think about that working out?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Roger, first of all, thank you for joining us today. I will start answering. Let's talk about capital allocation broader than just that. As we demonstrate in the last few quarters, we have a priority to have a consistent and growing dividend over time. We have demonstrated a few quarters now. The second priority is, we have outlined this quarter very specifically, is having a strong balance sheet, right? You probably can appreciate the major improvement that we have seen, that we have demonstrated on the DKL balance sheet. Obviously, the third point here is the buyback. I want to be clear, we see a lot of value in our share price today.
We elected not to do buybacks due to development in the strategic initiative progress. This is where we are on capital allocation. Obviously, you asked specifically about W2W. W2W always play in our toolbox that the asset develop very nicely in the last two years, and they're probably gonna receive the value of that asset going up, and it's a very premier midstream asset.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Yeah, no question about that. I guess, let me pivot a little bit just to the operational front. Big Spring, been doing a lot of work there. Where are we in this process? Halfway through, three-quarters of the way through? You know, it'll take a long time to do the last 10% of improvements there, but from a reliability and an OpEx standpoint, just how that's shaping up.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Roger. We definitely see improvement. Joseph is very close to that, so I will let him answer it.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yes. We are executing our plans in Big Spring, and as a result, we see the improved reliability that we expected, which allows us to meet our targets, like we communicated in the past. One, run around 70,000 barrels per day on a more consistent basis. It's not Q1, but it's starting to be real here with the guidance for the Q2. Second is improve our capture toward 70%, really on mid-cycle basis. And last is to improve our cost structure. We promised a $1 per barrel per quarter reduction until we get to the mid $5 per barrel target range by the end of the year. Very happy and proud with the team and the progress that we are making.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Manav Gupta with UBS. Please go ahead.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Hey, guys. My question is more on the DKL side as it relates to DK. You know, DKL continues to be bigger and bigger part of the earnings in the last five years. As DK looks at DKL, do you see with the Permian growth, you moving in a direction where the third-party EBITDA would just continue to grow and increase versus, you know, drop-downs or organic DK contribution to DKL? I mean, just trying to understand from this point on, should we expect the DKL to continue to grow with more and more third-party EBITDA in there?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. First of all, Manav, thank you for joining us today. It's a great question. We are very proud of the progress we did. Our first priority is both unitholders and shareholders, and the value that we are creating gonna find itself into those two pockets, and that's a priority for us. Obviously, we have demonstrated first to ourselves and then to the market that we can manage those assets and can show abnormal return on them. If the opportunity presents itself, as long as it's accretive for both DK and DKL, we'll take a good hard look into that and keep developing organically and inorganically.
The answer is to the bottom line, if the opportunity presents itself, and it's a good opportunity and it can benefit both units and shares, we'll take a good hard look at that.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Second quick question here is, look, quarter-over-quarter, three refineries showed pretty good improvement, Big Spring, Krotz Springs, and even El Dorado. I'm just trying to understand, is the kit getting to a point where you would like it to be? Obviously, there's a scope of improvement. If we look between Q4 and Q1 performance, what were some of the criteria which allowed these three assets to deliver much better earnings in Q1 versus just the last quarter?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, absolutely. Some of that is our doing, some of that is obviously the market that was better, and that's reflecting the capture rate. We obviously gave a clear guidance to the OpEx that shows better even in Q2 versus Q1. Joseph, why don't you chime in and give some more color into that?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. So far it has been mainly playing defense, right? In Q1, if you count the $3.50 per barrel LPO in Big Spring and the $1.50 per barrel headwind on the OpEx, this is $30 million that was left on the table related to the freeze events, right? To answer your question, as we have lost less and less surprises and headwind to deal with, we are more and more focused on transitioning to offense and optimize our business, thinking more about process optimization, selecting the right crude, making the right product, taking it to the right markets. At the end of the day, it will translate to a much better capture, and the market will get a chance to see the true profitability option of this system.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Thanks, guys, and congrats on a stronger quarter, and keep up the good work. Thank you.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Manav. Thank you again.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Paul Cheng with Scotiabank. Please go ahead.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Hi. Good morning, guys.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Morning, Paul.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Good morning, Paul.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Joseph, just curious. I mean, you get hit, as you mentioned earlier, that on this winter storm, Big Spring, you estimate that it's close to $5 impact, both in the profit margin as well as on the cost. Krotz Springs is another, say, 21.50 odd, right? Maybe I got it wrong, but also that have maybe at least $1.50 on the impact. What's the lesson that we learned from that? Is that something that you can do to prevent it? Because the winter storm is actually well telegraphed way beforehand. Is there anything operationally that we can do in order to minimize that kind of impact? That's the first question.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thank you for the question. First, I will correct one thing. The $1.50 per barrel in Krotz Springs was related to a planned catalyst cleaning in the coker unit, so we knew about it coming into the quarter. It has been a long cycle and to make it all the way to the turnaround and get you the maximum throughput through the driving season, we executed the scope in a low margin environment, and I'm very glad we did it. In Big Spring, it was really the typical challenges of freeze, right? I mean, frozen lines, instrumentation like our peers dealt with. What are we doing? What are the lessons? It's all about risk mitigation.
You think about people, process, equipment, and our main job here is to mitigate the risk each and every day and to better position the asset to deal with every possible challenge and whatever the market gives to us. Very proud of the team. Looking at Q2, we are ready to run, and I think good things are coming our way.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Second question. On the supply and marketing, you said that wholesale lost $60 million in the quarter. I think in the past, you sort of giving a kind of guidance saying that the wholesale will be doing roughly about $30 million a quarter, and our spot will be lower in Q1 and Q4, maybe at $5 million, and then in Q2 and Q3 will be somewhere in the $15 million. For a full year, about $40 million. Based on what we've seen in the last several quarters, is those guidance still a good one or that internally that you guys have built them somewhat differently?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I will start, Paul, with your permission, and then I will allow Joseph to give some more colors around that question. Great question. First of all, we need to start that wholesale is a strategic key part of a downstream integrated business unit. We see the value in that. We see our ability to place products in a different market conditions. We need to remember that when we are looking in wholesale, right? That's the first part. The second part, it's a bit more tricky to model wholesale because of the dynamic nature of that business. That business is changing every day, and the market are very dynamic. It's a bit. It's not as simple to model it, and that's the reason we are not giving always clear guidance about that.
I know that Joseph put a lot of thinking into that topic, so please.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Paul, first, to answer your question, I think the real answer is no. I mean, that range is probably not a good place to be. When you look at the full year 2023, supply and marketing still made +$50 million, right? So statistically, we averaged slightly over $10 million positive contribution per quarter. However, it's a very hard number to model. Like Avigal said, it's very important to realize we are an integrated downstream company, and the wholesale marketing is playing a strategic role to connect between our refineries to the customers. We move around 210,000 barrels per day of products through that wholesale marketing, which is approximately 800 million gallons per quarter.
High level, it takes a -7.5 cents per gallon margin between the pricing differential and RINs to get to a $60 million loss type of number. I'm sure you and others who follow the screen remember the -30, 35 cents per gallon back in January through the Midcon freeze. I think our team is doing great job in mitigating this risk going forward, diversifying our pricing exposure and footprint, and hopefully we're gonna do better in these type of situations in the future.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
All right. Will do. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line.[crosstalk]
Your next question will come from the line of John Royall with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. So I just had a follow-up on capital allocation. I guess it's a two-parter. One is, you've hiked your dividend now. I think seven quarters in a row, up 25% over that time period. Should we expect that to continue with the more frequent but smaller hikes, or will you get to the point where you move to more of a once-a-year type cadence? Then, the second part is just on the buyback, which you talked about the reasoning for turning it off in Q1. What's a reasonable expectation for when you might be back in the market for buybacks?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I will answer both of those questions more broadly, and I will not be as specific. As I said all along, being a shareholder-friendly company is a key priority for us, as long as maintaining a strong balance sheet. We definitely will maintain that. As I said, a few times, having a consistent and growing dividend over time is something that we value, and we believe our investors value as well. Both of them are very key priorities for us. Around the buyback, I want to make a point very clear. We've seen a lot of value in our share price, but we elected not to do it, because of developments in the strategic initiative and the progress we have made around it.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Great. Thank you. Can you talk about the timing of separating retail? I realize these processes don't just kick off overnight, but it's a little bit of a tougher time fundamentally now, at least over the short term, on fuel margin and also on merchandise sales. Do you think the enthusiasm for this business and the asset sale market is maybe what it was six or 12 months ago? Or do you think buyer expectations have adjusted at all?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, we obviously are not gonna be specific around the process. We have a great asset, a unique market position, a unique market. We are making good progress.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Okay. Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Ryan Todd with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Thank you. Maybe if we think about your refining EBITDA over the last four quarters, I think you've generated around $580 million of EBITDA in an environment that was generally above historical mid-cycle margins. As you think about your refining business going forward, what do you believe is the mid-cycle EBITDA or earnings power of the business as currently constituted? And how do you maybe think about the bridge of where it is versus where you want it to be, whether in terms of cost reductions, reliability improvements, ability to repatriate EBITDA out of DKL back into DK? Like, how do you want the market to think about, how should we be thinking about the mid-cycle earnings power of your refining business?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Ryan, thank you for the great question. As we said in the past, we believe that our earning power in refining is improving as we speak. We have seen better capture rates. You have seen that in all refineries, and we have seen that we demonstrate lower and lower LPO. That's a key part of that. Joseph put a lot of time into that, so maybe, Joseph, you want to take this one?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. We think on a mid-cycle basis, our mid-cycle EBITDA is between $750 to $800 million.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
At the refining level?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
No, this is for the entire company, and this is considering a stable refining segment with minimum surprises as we position it.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Okay. Perfect. Thank you. Maybe I guess it probably feeds into that some, but I don't know if I missed it earlier or not. Can you update us as to, like, progress to date on the cost reduction target? I know you talked about the $90 to $100 million, you know, kind of run rate for 2024. Are you there? Where have you seen the greatest improvement so far? What's worked well? What still remains to be done? Maybe just an update in terms of the process there.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Absolutely. We are focusing to be at around $90 to $100 billion exiting 2024. We have found additional opportunities in towards 2025, and that goes very well. Reuven and his team is doing an amazing job around it. Reuven, you wanna add anything?
Reuven Spiegel
EVP of Special Projects, Delek US Holdings
Well, we have executed most of the steps that we planned thus far. We have two more steps in Q2 and Q3 that will put us on track for $90 to $100 million. We have identified opportunities between $15 to $20 million that will be executed in 2025.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Great. Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Matthew Blair with TPH. Please go ahead.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Thank you and good morning. There's some reports that Wink-to-Webster will be offline in January for up to two weeks. Is that correct? And what kind of market impact would you anticipate? And if that did widen out Midland spreads, do you think Delek would be in a position to benefit there?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Matthew, thank you for the question. Obviously, I'm not gonna comment about W-to-W operation. We are not the operator of the line, and we are not commenting on those kind of rumors or news. Regarding the spread, I think that everyone can see that the Longhorn spread, i.e. Midland MEH, is widening pretty nicely. We see it in June widening all the way to $2.00 in H2. Q4, I think it's like $0.75 now. That's a demonstration of increase in production. We see the production in Midland 6.5, 6.6 million barrels per day, and probably gonna go up this year on the additional 250 to 300 thousand barrels a day.
That's put the Midland differentials going into the next half, which is the Basin and the Cushing. That's gonna widen the differential just a little bit. That's obviously a very good development for us.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Sounds good. Circling back to the commentary on supply and marketing,
You mentioned you're seeing some seasonal demand improvement. You're rolling off the very negative values in January, but we also see RINs, you know, 10% to 15% lower. Putting that all together, do you think supply and marketing can be positive EBITDA contribution in Q2 after the $65 million loss in Q1?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Matthew. It's still early in the quarter. We believe in the business, but I'm not gonna give guidance for that. We gave a lot of guidance that help you to model really well. It's really hard to predict the dynamic in the market at this second, so I'm gonna stay out of that guidance.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Okay. Sounds good. Thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Jason Gabelman with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Yeah. Hey, morning. Thanks for taking my questions. I wanted to go back to the marketing business and just how you're evaluating unlocking value there. I think when you started this value unlock process a little over a year ago, marketing was considered a core part of the business and wasn't something you were gonna look to really try to monetize, and it sounds like that's changed. Just wondering over the past year why that's changed.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Jason, thank you for the question. Obviously, our commitment, as I said many times, is to make sure that our investors see the value in both the unit price and the share price here. We are taking a good, hard look at everything, and that's something we decided that we need to look at the opportunities. I think that's what a prudent management needs to do, and that's what we are doing.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Okay, thanks. Yeah. Just, I guess, on the supply and trading line, as we think about it moving forward, and I know you wanna stay away from really providing concrete guidance, but I'm just wondering if you see any headwinds when your assets aren't operating at 100% and you try to buy product in the market to fulfill contractual obligations. Was that an impact in Q1, and is that something we could think about maybe not recurring moving forward?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I don't want to get into too much into the weeds here. Obviously, having a safe and reliable operation has a very broad benefits. There is a reason, Jason, that I'm very determined about the safe and reliable operation. That's actually priority. Without getting too much technicalities about how each one of the entity works with the other, I will just tell you that this is a commitment, and that's a priority, and we are driving a lot of energy into that, and I will leave it to that.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
All right. Thanks for the answers.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. I will now hand the call back to Avigal for any closing remarks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Thank you. So I want to thank our employees for their hard commitment for the success of this company. I want to thank you, shareholders, for trusting in us and the interest that you are showing around our business. I want to thank our loyal customers, and I want to thank our board of directors for their support, good advice, and commitment. Obviously, I want to thank my colleagues here around the table that's working days and nights in order to make this company what it is. Thank you, guys.
Operator
That will conclude today's conference. Thank you all for joining. You may now disconnect.
